A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain complete main text, Table 1, equations, and proof appendices. Corresponding content can be matched despite substantial reorganization, including v1 Appendices A–C becoming v2 Appendices B–D.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical convergence and classification-error results with proofs. Neither its main text nor appendices contain original experiments, simulations, or data analyses.

after.justification: v2 remains entirely theoretical, including the new polynomially tailed mixture results. Its appendices contain proofs and analytical comparisons, without original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same fixed-width, two-layer leaky ReLU network, fixed second-layer weights, exponential loss, and gradient descent on first-layer weights. The expanded distributional analysis does not introduce a different algorithm or architecture.

E1.justification: Neither version reports datasets or scenarios actually used in experiments. The added polynomially tailed mixture model is a theoretical distributional assumption, assessed under T1.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods experimentally. Table 1 summarizes prior theoretical guarantees; its revised citations do not constitute evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version contains an experimental evaluation protocol. Revised sample-size and parameter restrictions are mathematical sufficient conditions, rather than changes to measured evaluation settings.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, empirical robustness tests, sensitivity experiments, or case studies. The signal-regime and distributional extensions are theorem-based analyses covered under T1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. High-probability statements concern analytical guarantees over random samples, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Neither version reports measured scores, experimental rankings, or empirical qualitative findings. Changes concern analytical bounds and their implications, assessed under T1, C1, and C2.

T1.justification: v2 adds finite-r-moment mixtures with 2 < r <= 4, polynomial classification-error bounds, and Gaussian upper and lower bounds. Appendix C substantially revises the norm and alignment analysis to obtain two-sided control, while Appendix D.2 adds heavy-tail concentration and convergence arguments. Sufficient conditions also change. The earlier convergence results largely survive as Theorem 4.8 and Lemma 7.1; v1 Corollary 6.3 survives as Corollary A.1.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction expand the contributions from directional convergence and sub-Gaussian benign-overfitting guarantees to polynomially tailed mixtures, Gaussian lower bounds, tightness, and failure of benign overfitting despite convergence. The fixed-width and beyond-near-orthogonality claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the Gaussian lower bound as showing that the signal-strength phase transition is a property of the model, and identifies failure regimes despite directional convergence. Section 8 removes v1's specific conjectures about convergence under mere linear separability and least squares using only one label class. The limitation concerning unmodeled label noise remains.

D1.justification: The mathematical network and optimizer specification remains in Section 3. Neither version supplies experimental implementation instructions, hardware, runtimes, or code/data access information. Added parameter restrictions belong to the theoretical assumptions.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Cai et al. [2025] and Schechtman and Schreuder [2025], distinguishing their differentiability or late-stage assumptions from this work's convergence claim. Positioning also incorporates the new heavy-tail and lower-bound claims. Much of Appendix A's comparison with Xu and Gu [2023] already appeared in v1 Section 6.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around benign overfitting, and the related-work subsections reverse order. Directional-convergence theorems are consolidated, the activation-based result moves into the proof sketch, and the isotropic corollary and detailed prior-work comparison move to Appendix A. The classification-error proof is extensively reorganized.

P2.justification: Table 1 moves lower on page 3, merges the gradient-descent directional-convergence cells, and changes its first footnote. Equations and paragraphs are reformatted and reflowed, but both versions retain one table and no figures. v2 also introduces a visibly malformed expression in Assumption 6.1(a).

improvement.justification: The extensions could substantially improve applicability and characterize when benign overfitting fails, but central new guarantees contain unresolved inconsistencies. Theorem 5.1 gives a polynomial PM bound, whereas Appendix D.9 states an exponential bound using the sub-Gaussian parameter L, unavailable under PM. Lemma C.12 also propagates v1 Lemma B.10's missing one-half tail factor into the new Gaussian equality and lower bounds: its two-sided tail is used as a one-sided classification error. These issues prevent a reliable net quality judgment despite the broader analysis and clearer organization.
